{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on }} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka]] [[Category:History of Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Category:Buildings in Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Category:Atago shrines]] [[Category:Cherry blossom spots]] {{ill|Izanagi|en}}

}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka]] [[Category:History of Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Category:Buildings in Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Category:Atago shrines]] [[Category:Cherry blossom spots]] The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here [[every:Washio Atago Shrine|Washio Atago Shrine]] and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]][[en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
}} {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} [[ja:%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE]] == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} [[fr:Washio Atago-jinja]] ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} [[Category:Former Gōsha shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Fukuoka]] [[Category:History of Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Category:Buildings in Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Category:Atago shrines]] [[Category:Cherry blossom spots]]
