}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗}}’s Shugendō sect. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|12=draft}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|12=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|12=draft}}
}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft}}. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft}}. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|12=draft}}

}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft}}. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here [[every:Washio Atago Shrine|Washio Atago Shrine]] and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|12=draft}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|12=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|12=draft}}
}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft}}. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|12=draft}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|12=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|12=draft}}
}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft}}. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft}}. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft|12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|12=draft|12=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|12=draft|12=draft}}
}} {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{Interlanguage link|12=draft|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft|12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|12=draft|12=draft}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Green Space }} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=draft|12=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||12=draft|12=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|12=draft|12=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|12=draft|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=draft|12=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=draft|12=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=draft|12=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=draft|12=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=draft|12=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=draft|12=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=draft|12=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|12=draft|12=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|12=draft|12=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=draft|12=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|12=draft|12=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=draft|12=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=draft|12=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=draft|12=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=draft|12=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|12=draft|12=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=draft|12=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban }} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Green Space While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} [[Category:Completion tier 7]] {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Green Space {{神社 |画像=[[Image:Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg|250px]]
拝殿 |名称=鷲尾愛宕神社 |所在地=[[福岡県]][[福岡市]][[西区 (福岡市)|西区]][[愛宕 (福岡市)|愛宕]]2-7-1 |位置={{Coord|33|35|08|N|130|20|05|E|region:JP-40_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |祭神=[[伊耶那岐]]尊
[[アメノオシホミミ|天忍穂耳尊]]
[[カグツチ|火産霊神]]
[[イザナミ|伊耶那美尊]] |社格=旧[[郷社]]・[[別表神社]] |創建=[[景行天皇]]の治世 |例祭=[[9月23日]]・[[9月24日|24日]] |神事= |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Fukuoka city|label=鷲尾
愛宕神社|width=200|caption=}} }} '''鷲尾愛宕神社'''（わしおあたごじんじゃ）は、[[福岡県]][[福岡市]][[西区 (福岡市)|西区]][[愛宕 (福岡市)|愛宕]]の[[愛宕山]]（旧名 鷲尾山）にある[[神社]]である。旧[[社格]]は[[郷社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。単に「愛宕神社」とも呼ばれる。 [[イザナギ|伊耶那岐尊]]・[[アメノオシホミミ|天忍穂耳尊]]を祀る鷲尾神社（鷲尾権現）と、[[カグツチ|火産霊神]]・[[イザナミ|伊耶那美尊]]を祀る愛宕神社（愛宕権現）が明治時代に合併したものである。 眺望がよく、[[シーサイドももち|百道浜地区]]にも近いことから、百道浜地区が写っている写真はこの愛宕神社付近から撮影していることが多い。また、隠れデートスポットでもある。 『[[網走番外地 (東映)|網走番外地　悪への挑戦]]』、『[[ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）]]』『[[はなちゃんのみそ汁]]』など映画のロケ地としても知られる。 ==歴史== 神社の創始は[[景行天皇]]2年(西暦72年）、鷲尾山に[[イザナギ|伊耶那岐尊]]・[[アメノオシホミミ|天忍穂耳尊]]を祀ったのが鷲尾神社（鷲尾権現）の始まりとされる。鷲尾権現は英彦山権現と同神で、里人の説に曰く「初め英彦山権現自体も鷲尾山に祀られ、後に[[英彦山]]に移られた」ともいうが確たることは不詳である。 [[天暦]]9年、姪浜の住侶・浦左京という者が神社の破損を憂い、社殿改築の浄財を募ると、寄進の材木が山をなし崇敬者の労役奉仕が後を絶たなかったとされる。やがて鷲尾神社は鷲尾山の地主神として[[天台宗|天台]][[修験道|修験]]東林寺の[[社僧]]が管理するようになった。 鎌倉時代に入り元寇が起こると、幕府は博多に[[鎮西探題]]を設置し玄界灘を見渡せる当山に城砦（鷲尾城・探題城・姪浜城・浦城）を築城した。やがて[[後醍醐天皇]]の討幕運動が活発になると博多の探題館は九州の諸将に攻められて陥落。この際に鷲尾山の探題城も焼亡した。一説には探題・[[北条英時|赤橋英時]]が自刃したのもこの探題城であるといわれる。南北朝時代にも探題城には[[一色氏]]や[[渋川氏]]などが在城したが、度重なる兵火に見舞われた。このため社領・社宝・文書は失われるなど鷲尾神社も衰退し、ただ東林寺が残るのみであった。 江戸時代、[[福岡藩]]2代藩主[[黒田忠之]]が、[[黒田騒動]]を[[愛宕権現]]の霊験により乗り切ったことに感謝して、[[寛永]]11年（[[1634年]]）、京都の愛宕山白雲寺（現在の[[愛宕神社]]）より愛宕権現（[[イザナミ|伊耶那美尊]]・[[カグツチ|火産霊神]]）を勧請し、鷲尾権現のある鷲尾山に祀り、20余石4人扶持、山林1万坪、預かり山4万坪の社領が藩より奉祀された『愛宕神社物語』という。これにより鷲尾権現は愛宕権現の境内末社とされた。ともに[[真言宗]]円満寺によって管理され、[[宝暦]]年間（[[1751年]] - [[1764年]]）には東林寺も廃止された。山自体も愛宕山と呼ばれるようになった。 明治34年（[[1901年]]）9月27日、「鷲尾神社は末社となすべき神社にあらざる」を以って両社を合併して鷲尾愛宕神社とした。大正2年（[[1913年]]）3月19日に村社『福岡縣神社誌』に定められ、昭和6年（[[1931年]]）7月10日には郷社となる。戦後は神社本庁の別表神社に加列した。現在でも火徳の神、願掛け（断事）の神として遠近の参詣多く、正月3ヶ日には70万人『愛宕神社だより』もの参拝があるなど、福岡県内有数の参拝者数を誇る神社である。 [[画像:Night view of Fukuoka from Atago jinja.jpg|thumb|350px|鷲尾愛宕神社からの夜景]] ==愛宕山ケーブルカー== 1928年に[[愛宕索道]]が設立され、全国で二番目にして九州初となるロープウェイが建設された。その後[[1928年]]から[[1943年]]まで、麓の明治通り([[国道202号]])から愛宕山山頂までを結ぶ[[ロープウェイ]]が営業していた。参拝者、観光客、修学旅行の学生達等が訪れ大変賑わっていた。しかし、[[第二次世界大戦]]中の1943年、ロープ・ワイヤー・車体を供出することになり廃止された。神社近くの茶店横に愛宕山ケーブルカーを記念したパネルが設置されている。 ==桜の名所== 春はおよそ「2千本の桜」が咲く桜の名所として有名で、桜の季節になると境内外は多くの花見客で賑わう。 == アクセス == *[[福岡市地下鉄空港線]][[室見駅]]より徒歩12分（約980m） *[[天神 (福岡市)|天神地区]]より[[西鉄バス]]301・302・333系統に乗車し「愛宕神社入口」バス停で下車、徒歩10分（860m） *[[福岡高速環状線]][[愛宕出入口]]より約1㎞。 == 脚注 == {{Reflist}} == 外部リンク == * [http://atagojinja.com 福岡市・愛宕神社公式サイト] * [http://www.kaiun-goriyaku.com/40j-017.htm 全国開運神社仏閣ガイド] * [http://www.city.fukuoka.jp/contents/7d2dcc85b/7d2dcc85b6.htm 福岡市サイト] {{神道 横}} {{shinto-stub}} {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} {{DEFAULTSORT:わしおあたこしんしや}} [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:福岡県の旧郷社]] [[Category:福岡市の神社]] [[Category:福岡市西区の歴史]] [[Category:福岡市西区の建築物]] [[Category:愛宕神社]] [[Category:桜に関する場所]]

It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here [[every:Washio Atago Shrine|Washio Atago Shrine]] and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} [[Category:Completion tier 7]] {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline.
