The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Green Space Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:26, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Green Space Conservation District Atago 2 and 3-chōme Nishi-ku Fukuoka 20230224.jpg|alt=愛宕山特別緑地保全地区|Atago-yama Special Green Space Conservation District File:Back view of Haiden and Honden of Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=拝殿と本殿の背面|Back View of Haiden and Honden Five-storied pagoda in the keidai of Washio-Atago-jinja 7-1 Atago 2-chōme Nishi-ku Fukuoka 20221220.jpg|alt=五重塔|Five-storied Pagoda File:Fushimi Inari Shrine and Unome Inari Shrine in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=伏見稲荷神社と鵜ノ目稲荷神社|Fushimi Inari Shrine and Unome Inari Shrine File:Gate of Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=門|Gate File:Gojunoto Tower in Washio-Atago Shrine.jpg|alt=五重塔|Gojunoto Tower File:Grand torii of Washio-Atago Shrine.jpg|alt=大鳥居|Grand Torii File:Haiden of Otojiro Inari Shrine on Mount Atagoyama.JPG|alt=拝殿|Haiden of Otojiro Inari Shrine File:Honden and sacred cattle in Washio-Atago Shrine.jpg|alt=本殿と神聖な牛|Honden and Sacred Cattle File:Jizoin Temple on sando of Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=地蔵院|Jizoin Temple on Sando File:Memorial trees in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=記念樹|Memorial Trees File:Muromigawa River from Washio-Atago Shrine.jpg|alt=室見川|Muromigawa River View File:Observation Area of Mount Atago in the precincts of Atagojinja 7-1 Atago-2-chōme Nishi-ku Fukuoka City 20221006.jpg|alt=愛宕山展望エリア|Observation Area of Mount Atago File:Okunoin Shrine of Otojiro Inari Shrine on Mount Atagoyama.JPG|alt=奥の院|Okunoin Shrine File:Pigeons in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=鳩|Pigeons File:Roof of Haiden of Otojiro Inari Shrine on Mount Atagoyama.JPG|alt=拝殿の屋根|Roof of Haiden File:Sacred cattle in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=神聖な牛|Sacred Cattle File:Sacred horse in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=神聖な馬|Sacred Horse File:Sando of Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=参道|Sando File:Shimmon Gate of Washio-Atago Shrine from Shrine.jpg|alt=伏見稲荷と鵜ノ目稲荷の鳥居|Toriis of Fushimi Inari and Unome Inari Shrine File:Uga Shrine in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=宇賀神社|Uga Shrine File:Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg|alt=拝殿|Haiden ==See }} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Green Space The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja||qq=draft|qq=draft}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban }} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko|qq=}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenryaku era|qq=}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tendai Buddhism|qq=}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamakura period|qq=}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Domain|qq=}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromi Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka City Subway|qq=}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Urban Expressway|qq=}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo Shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko|qq=}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenryaku era|qq=}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tendai Buddhism|qq=}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamakura period|qq=}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Domain|qq=}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromi Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka City Subway|qq=}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Urban Expressway|qq=}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo Shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|ja|神社本庁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|ja|英彦山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko|qq=}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku era|ja|天暦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenryaku era|qq=}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tendai Buddhism|ja|天台宗|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tendai Buddhism|qq=}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|ja|鎌倉時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamakura period|qq=}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Edo period|qq=}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|ja|福岡藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Domain|qq=}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|ja|室見駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Muromi Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|ja|福岡市地下鉄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka City Subway|qq=}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Urban Expressway|ja|福岡高速環状線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Urban Expressway|qq=}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=}}

}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
