}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka The imported history from everybodywiki is patchwork and contains all the contributing users, but not all the revisions are actually present. Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=see for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:26, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=page was originally created in the draft namespace on english wikipedia. It was then copied to userspace on simple english wikipedia and edited before being imported here. The entire simple english wikipedia history is present, but the wikipedia draft can be found on everybodywiki here and should be undeleted here on wikipedia [[:en:draft:Washio Atago Shrine]] and have the revisions imported to this wiki to give proper attribution. While most edits are by Immanuelle there might be a few from other users. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special }} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}

}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|Fukuoka Urban Expressway]]. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} ==Gallery== File:Atago-Jizo Hall in Washio-Atago Shrine.JPG|alt=愛宕地蔵堂|Atago-Jizo Hall File:Atago-yama Special [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 09:35, 18 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{infobox shinto shrine | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | image = Washio-Atago Shrine Haiden.jpg |deity={{ill|Atago Gongen|ja|Atago Gongen|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Gongen|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}
{{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka]] [[:en:Japan|Japan]]. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]], Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|lt=Ken-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#District_shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}, it is currently registered as a [[:en:Beppyo shrine|Beppyo Shrine]] under the [[:en:Association of Shinto Shrines|Association of Shinto Shrines]]. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|qq=}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|qq=}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|qq=}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to [[:en:Mount Hiko|Mount Hiko]]. In the ninth year of the [[:en:Tenryaku|Tenryaku era]], a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|qq=}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from [[:en:Tiantai|Tendai Buddhism]]’s Shugendō sect. During the [[:en:Kamakura period|Kamakura period]], the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]], the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩}} of the [[:en:Fukuoka Domain|Fukuoka Domain]], {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|qq=}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|qq=}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from [[:en:Muromi Station|Muromi Station]] on the [[:en:Fukuoka City Subway|Fukuoka City Subway]] Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|qq=}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the [[:en:Fukuoka There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine.
