The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|1=Seaside Momochi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11308788}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|1=Non-ko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11325822}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|1=Hanachan no Misoshiru|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q18338857}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q462555}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|en|Mount Hiko|WD=Q3077886|lt=Mount Hiko|1=Mount Hiko}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku|en|Tenryaku|WD=Q1346281|lt=Tenryaku era|1=Tenryaku}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|1=Meinohama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447357}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|WD=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism|1=Tiantai}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩|1=Han system|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q841985}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|en|Fukuoka Domain|WD=Q208766|lt=Fukuoka Domain|1=Fukuoka Domain}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|1=Tadayuki Kuroda|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11678600}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|en|Muromi Station|WD=Q4357442|lt=Muromi Station|1=Muromi Station}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|en|Fukuoka City Subway|WD=Q289242|lt=Fukuoka City Subway|1=Fukuoka City Subway}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|1=Nishitetsu Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11629843}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|en|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|WD=Q11592981|lt=Fukuoka Urban Expressway|1=Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q462555}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|WD=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism|1=Tiantai}}’s Shugendō sect. {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}}
{{ill|Ame-no-oshihomimi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-oshihomimi|qq=}}
{{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagu-tsuchi|qq=}}
{{ill|Izanami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
}} {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|en|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|WD=Q1132402|lt=Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|1=Nishi-ku, Fukuoka}} {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}. It is a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a shrine that is particularly notable in a certain way with a significant history to it.{{Cite web |title=別表神社とは？御朱印めぐりに参考になる「別表神社一覧」とマップ {{!}} 開運戦隊ゴシュインジャー |url=https://jinja-gosyuin.com/beppyou/ |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=jinja-gosyuin.com}} It is One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines{{Cite web |last=HN |date=2023-06-21 |title=Washio Atago Shrine – One of Japan’s Three Great Atago Shrines |url=https://visitjapan-vegetarian.com/washio-atago-shrine-one-of-japans-three-great-atago-shrines/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |language=en-US}}. There are about 900 shrines in the network.{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110517220742/http://kyoto-atago.jp/images/yuishogaki2.htm|access-date=2024-03-27|website=web.archive.org}} It is headed by the Kyoto shrine. It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q462555}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|1=Seaside Momochi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11308788}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|1=Non-ko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11325822}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|1=Hanachan no Misoshiru|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q18338857}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q462555}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|en|Mount Hiko|WD=Q3077886|lt=Mount Hiko|1=Mount Hiko}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku|en|Tenryaku|WD=Q1346281|lt=Tenryaku era|1=Tenryaku}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|1=Meinohama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447357}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|WD=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism|1=Tiantai}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩|1=Han system|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q841985}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|en|Fukuoka Domain|WD=Q208766|lt=Fukuoka Domain|1=Fukuoka Domain}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|1=Tadayuki Kuroda|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11678600}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|en|Muromi Station|WD=Q4357442|lt=Muromi Station|1=Muromi Station}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|en|Fukuoka City Subway|WD=Q289242|lt=Fukuoka City Subway|1=Fukuoka City Subway}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|1=Nishitetsu Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11629843}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|en|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|WD=Q11592981|lt=Fukuoka Urban Expressway|1=Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} It was built in the year 72.{{Cite web |last=Inoue |first=Mai |date=2021-03-01 |title=Cherry Blossoms and Beautiful Night Views at Atago Shrine |url=http://www.fukuoka-now.com/en/cherry-blossoms-and-beautiful-night-views-at-atago-shrine/ |access-date=2023-10-19 |website=Fukuoka Now |language=en-US}} == Three Great Atago shrines == This is one of the three great Atago shrines. The other ones are round in diverse locations.{{Cite web|date=2013-04-19|title=Atago Shrine - Fukuoka|url=https://en.japantravel.com/fukuoka/atago-shrine/4255|access-date=2024-03-27|website=JapanTravel|language=en}} # {{ill|Washio Atago Shrine|ja|%E9%B7%B2%E5%B0%BE%E6%84%9B%E5%AE%95%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE|simple|User:Immanuelle/Washio_Atago_Shrine|en:draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Washio Atago Shrine|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Tokyo)|qq=}} # {{ill|Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Shrine (Kyoto)|qq=}} Head of the network. === Lesser Atago Shrines === #{{ill|Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|lt=Atago Shrine|ja|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun (Mito)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} # {{ill|Atagoyama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atagoyama Kofun|qq=}} ==Overview== '''Washio Atago Shrine''' (鷲尾愛宕神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located on {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}} (formerly Washio Mountain) in {{ill|Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja|福岡市西区|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishi-ku, Fukuoka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}, Japan. Formerly classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}, it is currently registered as a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|en|Beppyo shrine|WD=Q10898274|lt=Beppyo Shrine|1=Beppyo shrine}} under the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|WD=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. It is often referred to simply as "Atago Shrine." The shrine enshrines {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q462555}} (Washio Shrine/Washio Gongen) along with {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|ja|火産霊神|1=Kagu-tsuchi|lt=Kagutsuchi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagutsuchi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to カグツチ}} and {{ill|Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那美尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Atago Shrine/Atago Gongen). The two shrines were merged during the Meiji period. Due to its excellent vantage point and proximity to the {{ill|Momochi Seaside|ja|シーサイドももち|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momochi Seaside|1=Seaside Momochi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11308788}} area, many photographs of the region are taken from this shrine. It is also a popular hidden dating spot. The shrine has been featured as a filming location for movies such as ''{{ill|Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja|網走番外地　悪への挑戦|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abashiri Prison Challenge to Evil|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', ''{{ill|Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|ja|ノン子36歳（家事手伝い）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nonko 36 (Housekeeping Assistant)|1=Non-ko|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11325822}}'', and ''{{ill|Hana’s Miso Soup|ja|はなちゃんのみそ汁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana’s Miso Soup|1=Hanachan no Misoshiru|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q18338857}}''. == History == The shrine was first established in the second year of Emperor Keikō’s reign (72 CE), when {{ill|Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja|伊耶那岐尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja|天忍穂耳尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Oshihomimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノオシホミミ|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q462555}} were enshrined on Washio Mountain. Known as Washio Shrine (Washio Gongen), it was said to be associated with the same deity as {{ill|Mount Hiko Shrine|ja|英彦山権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Hiko Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, and local tradition claims that the Hiko deity was originally worshiped here before being relocated to {{ill|Mount Hiko|en|Mount Hiko|WD=Q3077886|lt=Mount Hiko|1=Mount Hiko}}. In the ninth year of the {{ill|Tenryaku|en|Tenryaku|WD=Q1346281|lt=Tenryaku era|1=Tenryaku}}, a local named Ura Saikyō from {{ill|Meinohama|ja|姪浜|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meinohama|1=Meinohama|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11447357}} took initiative to repair the shrine, gathering donations and materials. Washio Shrine later became a tutelary shrine managed by monks from {{ill|Tiantai|en|Tiantai|WD=Q668188|lt=Tendai Buddhism|1=Tiantai}}’s Shugendō sect. During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|WD=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period|1=Kamakura period}}, the shrine was affected by the Mongol invasions, as the government built a fortress on Washio Mountain. After enduring several battles, including the collapse of the Kamakura shogunate, the shrine was left in decline. In the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|WD=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}, the second {{ill|daimyō|ja|藩主|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/daimyō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 藩|1=Han system|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q841985}} of the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|en|Fukuoka Domain|WD=Q208766|lt=Fukuoka Domain|1=Fukuoka Domain}}, {{ill|Kuroda Tadayuki|ja|黒田忠之|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Tadayuki|1=Tadayuki Kuroda|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11678600}}, enshrined deities from {{ill|Atago Mountain|ja|愛宕山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Atago Mountain|1=Mount Atago|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11493827}} in Kyoto to express gratitude for overcoming the {{ill|Kuroda Incident|ja|黒田騒動|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuroda Incident|qq=}}. These deities were combined with Washio Gongen, forming the modern Washio Atago Shrine. == Atago Mountain Cable Car == In 1928, a ropeway was established, becoming the second in Japan and the first in Kyushu. It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|en|Muromi Station|WD=Q4357442|lt=Muromi Station|1=Muromi Station}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|en|Fukuoka City Subway|WD=Q289242|lt=Fukuoka City Subway|1=Fukuoka City Subway}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|1=Nishitetsu Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11629843}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|en|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|WD=Q11592981|lt=Fukuoka Urban Expressway|1=Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route}}. {{Commonscat|Washio-Atago-jinja}} It operated until 1943 when it was dismantled during World War II. A commemorative panel near the shrine marks its history. == Famous for Cherry Blossoms == With approximately "2,000 cherry trees," the shrine is renowned as a popular spot for hanami (flower viewing) in spring. == Access == * 12-minute walk from {{ill|Muromi Station|en|Muromi Station|WD=Q4357442|lt=Muromi Station}} on the {{ill|Fukuoka City Subway|en|Fukuoka City Subway|WD=Q289242|lt=Fukuoka City Subway}} Airport Line. * 10-minute walk from the "Atago Shrine Entrance" bus stop on {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus|ja|西鉄バス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11629843}} routes 301, 302, and 333. * 1 km from the Atago Interchange on the {{ill|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|en|Fukuoka Expressway Circular Route|WD=Q11592981|lt=Fukuoka Urban
